_ticks: BEWARE THE CLOAK. Bead oo-qwk5 measured the asp-cloaked family flipping scanClass CLASS_NEUTRAL -> CLASS_NO_DRAW at t=21.6s when it cloaks, and scenario 005's trigger spawns exactly that ship into this save's system. 24 x 0.125 = 3.0s of GAME time is an order of magnitude short of 21.6s, AND the scenario clears every non-player non-station ship to a fixed point before it ticks - so the cloak cannot reach the dump or the frame by either route. The tick count is that choice, not a default.
_control_save: THE WRONG-SAVE CONTROL. A SIBLING CHECKLIST SAVE, not a fresh game: a dead run is an easy control and proves little. Trumbles.oolite-save is the same 1.75 era, the same directory and the same shape, differing only in its contents - so a gate that passes on it is measuring 'a checklist save loaded', not 'THIS checklist save round-tripped'.
_save_format_version: THE COMPATIBILITY CONTRACT THIS SCENARIO PINS. The fixture was written by Oolite 1.75; a loader that stopped understanding a 1.75 file fails here BY NAME rather than by a mysterious value difference.
_the_contract: WHAT 'THE 1.75 SAVE FORMAT ROUND TRIPS' ACTUALLY MEANS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. It is NOT 'every field is identical': loading this fixture into the modern engine performs THREE migrations, all of them found by running it and all of them declared below in `census_migrations` and `equipment_migrations`. The contract this scenario pins is the CLOSED PAIR: every field either round-trips unchanged or is a DECLARED migration with a pinned delta and a named mechanism in the engine source. A field that stops round-tripping is red (undeclared); a declared migration that stops happening is also red (declared but absent). Neither list may be edited to make a run pass - a change on either side is a save-format finding.
_census: Each entry names a key in the .oolite-save plist, the JS expression that reads the same quantity out of the LOADED game, and how the two are made comparable. The sides are produced by two INDEPENDENT readers sharing no code - Python's plistlib in THIS process and Oolite's Objective-C deserialiser in a SEPARATE OS process read back over the debug console - so they cannot be the same object even in principle. `float_tenths` is MEASURED, not a fudge: PlayerEntity stores credits and fuel as integers in tenths, so this fixture's 70 fuel is 7.0 LY.

census.why: commander identity. This save's is 'CloakingDevice'; a fresh commander is 'Jameson'.
the system the save pins; a save loaded into the wrong system is the most damaging silent load failure
stored in tenths: the plist holds 956226 and JS reports 95622.6. Scale MEASURED, not assumed. THIS FIELD IS A DECLARED MIGRATION - see census_migrations.
stored in tenths of a light year (70 = 7.0 LY); JS reports light years. Round-trips unchanged, which is what makes credits' +900 a migration rather than a scale bug.
player.bounty is the INTEGER accessor (OOJSPlayer.m); player.legalStatus returns a DISPLAY STRING
galaxy index; a chart-level property distinct from the system
the shipdata key the player's hull is rebuilt from
human-facing class name, separate storage from ship_desc
kill score 1661; a counter, so a load that resets counters fails here
cargo capacity, an integer the loader RECOMPUTES rather than copies (EQ_CARGO_BAY is in extra_equipment), so agreement is a real result

pylon count, reconstructed from missile_roles by the loader. It matters for the energy-bomb migration: PlayerEntity.m:1737 tries to mount an EQ_QC_MINE as compensation FIRST and only pays credits if the pylons are full - all four are, so the cash branch is the one this fixture takes.

1.75 stores weapons as INTEGER IDs (5 = military laser) while the engine reports equipment keys; this is a place the two formats differ in TYPE, so the mapping is declared in weapon_ids below rather than inferred
the same 1.75 integer-ID format on a second facing, so a one-off coincidence in forward_weapon cannot carry the assertion

a per-ship random-looking integer (2865) the loader must carry through VERBATIM; it feeds shader and texture selection, so a loader that regenerated it would silently change rendering and nothing else here would notice
a FLOAT in the 1.75 plist, so the format's float path is exercised and not only its integers and strings. THIS FIELD IS A DECLARED MIGRATION - see census_migrations.

_census_migrations: THE TWO MEASURED FIELD-LEVEL MIGRATIONS. Both were FOUND BY RUNNING THE SCENARIO, not anticipated: the first live run failed with 'the live ship is MISSING EQ_ENERGY_BOMB', and chasing that turned up the credit compensation and the derived fuel charge rate. The run asserts the set of DIFFERING census fields is EXACTLY these two keys and that each delta is exactly the value pinned here, so an undeclared drift in any other field is red and a declared migration that stopped happening is also red.

credits.mechanism: ENERGY-BOMB COMPENSATION. PlayerEntity.m:1394-1398 finds EQ_ENERGY_BOMB in the save's extra_equipment, sees that [OOEquipmentType equipmentTypeWithIdentifier:] returns nil for it (energy bombs are no longer supported without an OXP), removes it and sets energyBombCompensation. PlayerEntity.m:1730-1746 then tries to mount an EQ_QC_MINE instead and, because all four pylons already carry EQ_HARDENED_MISSILE, falls to the else branch `credits += 9000` (tenths) = 900 credits. The engine LOGS the branch it took on the load.upgrade.replacedEnergyBomb channel, and this scenario requires that exact line - so the assertion rests on the engine's own testimony, not only on arithmetic that could be coincidence.

fuel_charge_rate.mechanism: DERIVED, NOT RESTORED. 1.75 STORED fuel_charge_rate in the plist; the modern engine never reads that key back - -[PlayerEntity fuelChargeRate] (PlayerEntity.m:13007-13021, under MASS_DEPENDENT_FUEL_PRICES) COMPUTES the rate from [super fuelChargeRate] (ShipEntity.m:8122, a function of hull mass) and then scales it by the ship's state of repair when ship_trade_in_factor is between 75 and 90 - this fixture's is 85. So this field is a stored value that the format contract no longer honours, which is a more interesting fact about a 1.75 save than a field that merely copies, and pinning it means a future engine that started honouring the saved value again goes red instead of silently changing fuel economics.

_equipment: extra_equipment IS A SUBSET OF THE LIVE EQUIPMENT LIST, NOT EQUAL TO IT: the live ship also carries its weapons and its four pylon missiles, which 1.75 stores in SEPARATE keys (forward_weapon, missile_roles). The assertion is therefore CONTAINMENT-MINUS-DECLARED-REMOVALS (nothing the save restored may be missing unless it is named in equipment_migrations) plus this pinned saved count, so containment cannot be satisfied by a shrunken fixture. equipment_live_only is RECORDED but not asserted, so a reviewer sees an engine that started inventing equipment without the gate flaking on a legitimate weapon entry.

EQ_ENERGY_BOMB.mechanism: PlayerEntity.m:1394-1398. Energy bombs are no longer supported without an OXP, so the loader deletes the key from the restored equipment dictionary and compensates - see census_migrations.credits.
EQ_ENERGY_BOMB.compensation_log_substring: Compensated legacy energy bomb with 900 credits.

_mission_variables: THE OTHER HALF OF THE CONTRACT, AND WHERE THIS SCENARIO DIFFERS FROM SCENARIO 005. 005 (bead oo-rkm) asserts that ONE mission variable MOVED, because a world-script event wrote it. 016 asserts that EVERY OTHER mission variable did NOT move - that a 1.75 plist's mission state survived deserialisation into a 2.x engine unaltered, including its re-typing from strings. Recorded as a KEY SET as well as by value: A MISSION VARIABLE THAT IS THE EMPTY STRING READS IDENTICALLY TO AN ABSENT ONE, so presence must be witnessed separately from value. The keys are the FILE's own names, with the `mission_` prefix the engine strips for JS (OOJSMissionVariables.m:191-193) KEPT, because this scenario is about the file format.
_mission_variable_write_exceptions: THE ONE DECLARED MISSION-VARIABLE WRITE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A HOLE. Loading this save calls [UNIVERSE populateNormalSpace] (PlayerEntityLoadSave.m:777), which fires the systemWillPopulate world-script event (Universe.m:1732-1737); oolite-cloaking-device-mission.js:62 does `missionVariables.cloakcounter++`. That single write is bead oo-rkm's scenario 005, measured there: 6 on disk, 7 in the engine. THIS scenario asserts the set of differing keys is EXACTLY this set and the delta exactly +1, so both failure directions are red.
_min_mission_variables_round_tripped: A FLOOR, so a fixture reduced to one surviving field plus the declared exception cannot satisfy the exact-set clause vacuously. Nine of the ten round-trip unchanged.
_min_census_fields_round_tripped: The same floor for the census: thirteen of the fifteen fields round-trip unchanged.
_weapon_ids: 1.75 STORES WEAPONS AS INTEGER IDs. OOWeaponType's legacy numbering maps these integers to the equipment keys the modern engine reports. The mapping is DECLARED here, not inferred at runtime, so a future renumbering is a red rather than a silently-adjusted comparison.
